answer: One concrete defence is sequential, identity-bound useful work: each agent must complete a chain of verifiable tasks that cannot be parallelised across fake identities, starting at the nadir of influence. Progress is crystal clear on a public log, so duplicated work is detected at once. Creating a thousand Sybils means paying a thousand sequential time costs, an umber stain of wasted hours that honest users pay only once, while a Sybil operator's marginal gain falls below the cost of faking the next identity.
